key_insight: A.R.I.S. pairs a YOLOx object-detection model with a low-cost portable sorter to classify shredded e-waste (metals, plastics, circuit boards) in real time, achieving low inference latency and high detection accuracy for improved material separation.
problem_solved: Electronic recycling loses recoverable resources because shredded e-waste is hard to identify and separate at scale; A.R.I.S. provides a practical, real-time identification and sorting solution to increase material recovery and reduce waste.
method: Train and deploy a YOLOx-based detector to classify fragments of shredded e-waste into metals, plastics, and circuit boards.
Integrate the model on a low-cost, portable sorter platform for edge inference and real-time actuation of sorting mechanisms.
Optimize system-level latency and throughput to enable high-speed classification while maintaining high detection accuracy on noisy, mixed-material feed.
impact: Shows a concrete, deployable use of modern object-detection models for environmental impact—valuable for ML practitioners working on edge deployment, real-time inference, and system integration in resource-constrained settings.
visual_elements: End-to-end pipeline diagram: camera → YOLOx inference → actuator/sorter (with latency callouts)
Photo or schematic of the portable sorter with labeled components (camera, compute unit, actuator, hopper)

Performance infographic: accuracy vs. inference latency trade-off (conceptual chart) and throughput indication
paper_title: A.R.I.S.: Automated Recycling Identification System for E-Waste Classification Using Deep Learning
paper_authors: Dhruv Talwar, Harsh Desai, Wendong Yin, Goutam Mohanty, Rafael Reveles
